text:
ashleigh: Heads up — OSS scanner flagged a vuln in kms-java-client. CVE-2026-0421. PoC circulating. Affects key wrap/token refresh path we use for hosted KMS proxies. Need to decide: emergency hotfix for hosted, backport to 1.2.x LTS, or schedule in next patch window? Impact touches Hosted + Dedicated customers using KMS integration. Thoughts?

marta: link to advisory: https://nvd.example.org/CVE-2026-0421 — severity: HIGH, remote exploit on auth refresh.

leo: If PoC exists, treat hosted as P1. We should push patched client to hosted runtime ASAP. For Dedicated/Private, customers may be pinned to images — offer backport/patch instructions.

sam: SLA question — will patch cause downtime? We have 99.9% for hosted standard tiers.

ashleigh: Hosted can do rolling restart with zero downtime if we do canary + live reload. Proposed rollout: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m. If any errors, auto-roll back. No planned downtime.

ops-sre-bot: @channel deploy job queued: job/patch-kms-client-2026-0421 started (canary 10%). Logs: `kubectl set image deployment/kms-proxy kms-proxy=redwood/kms-proxy:1.2.4-hotfix`

marta: For Dedicated customers: recommend three options to customers: 1) immediate managed backport (we patch their reserved pool), 2) self-apply patch with instructions, 3) temporary mitigation: rotate service keys + disable token refresh on proxy (config flag).

leo: Audit logging note — enable `kms.client.auth.debug=true` for 24h on canary to capture auth failures, then revert. Also ensure KMS key usage audit events are shipped to customer audit log (esp. enterprise).

sam: Public exposure risk: high if exploit can get wrapped keys. We should prepare a customer comms draft for enterprise & Dedicated within next 6h. Add legal/CS.

ashleigh: Suggested timelines: Hosted hotfix complete in 24h. Dedicated managed backports: offer within 72h, opt-in for earlier. Private / on-prem: notify immediately, provide patch + instructions, coordinate with CS for scheduling (could be >7 days depending on customer change windows).

security-bot: Vulnerability tracker updated: RED-SEC-2026-108. Severity HIGH. Assigned to @ashleigh, @leo. Mitigation flags: hotfix_in_progress, customer_notified_pending.

marta: Quick patch commands for customers (example):
```
# maven
mvn dependency:get -Dartifact=com.redwood:kms-client:1.2.4
# or gradle
implementation 'com.redwood:kms-client:1.2.4'
```

leo: Also include RBAC check: ensure service account used by kms-proxy has no write perms to key metadata. Limit to encrypt/decrypt only. Add post-patch audit: `SELECT * FROM audit_logs WHERE component='kms-proxy' AND action='key-update'`

ashleigh: Action items: @marta prepare customer email templates for Dedicated/Enterprise; @leo run the canary audit and confirm logs within 2h; @sam loop in CS/legal for messaging. I will monitor deploy and open incident channel if rollback triggered.

sam: I'll draft the enterprise notice and share in #security-commms in 1h.

marta: Starting customer outreach list now, will flag customers with HSM/private key stores first.

ops-sre-bot: Canary at 10% passed QA checks. Proceeding to 50% in 12m.

ashleigh: Thanks. Keep updates short in this thread. If we see any confirmed exploitation, escalate to incident response and consider temporary rate-limit on KMS endpoints. :warning:

leo: Noted. Will also add a short FAQ for support engineers on key rotation steps.

security-bot: Reminder: log retention for this event set to 90 days and audit exported to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incident-archive/RED-SEC-2026-108`.
